methodology: The study used small samples (45×45×900mm) subjected to a four-point bending test. Glass-Fiber-Reinforced Polymer (GFRP), Carbon-Fiber-Reinforced Polymer (CFRP), and Ultra-High-Modulus CFRPsheets were tested for reinforcement.
research_objective: To analyze the feasibility of reinforcing laminated veneer lumber panels with composite materials bonded to their exterior surfaces using epoxy resin.

key_findings.finding: Reinforcement with composite materials (GFRP, CFRP, UHMCFRP) positively affected the mechanical properties of laminated veneer lumber panels.
The bending stiffness increased significantly when reinforced with CFRP and UHMCFRP compared to GFRP.
The cost of reinforcement should consider not only the cost of FRP but also other factors such as required time, space, and equipment for application.
Local damage can be mitigated by limiting reinforcement scope to local areas.
Laminated veneer lumber (LVL) has better mechanical properties compared to solid timber.
The moisture content of LVL samples was measured after bending tests using a TanelWRD-100 electrofusion moisture meter, with an average value presented in Table 1.
The mechanical properties (modulus of elasticity, tensile strength) and physical properties (fiber mass, sheet mass, density) vary significantly between GFRP, CFRP, and UHM materials.
